text:
anya: Heads-up — seeing 200–400ms tail latency spikes on long-context streams. Correlates with cache reclamation runs on busy hosts.
liam: Which hosts + is there a small repro?
anya: prod-gpu-7 and staging repro with long-context-flood (ctx=65k tokens).
anya: pasted a quick perf sample snippet:```
# perf top (aggregate)
45.2% kv_reclaimer::wait_on_pager
18.3% kv_cache::page_in
10.7% runtime::schedule
6.1% memcpy
```
prashant: Hmm — that wait_on_pager number is huge. Did we flip reclaim policy recently?
julia: We moved to FIFO reinserts to reduce fragmentation last month. The reuse window is still 2s.
corey: My suspicion: under sustained long contexts FIFO reinserts + aggressive reclaimer cause hot entries to be paged while in-flight requests try to reuse them -> serialized page-ins and stalls.
liam: Can you try increasing reuse_window and/or backing off reclaimer frequency on staging? Quick A/B to confirm.
anya: Did that: bumped reuse_window 2s -> 8s on staging. Result: tail latency dropped ~3x in the stress run but resident mem climbed ~12% over 30m.
julia: Tradeoff expected. We need correctness and perf. Also worried about FIFO reinserts corrupting ordering assumptions for certain KV lookups — any evidence?
prashant: No data yet. Suggest adding a debug invariant in debug builds: when reinserting verify seq/timestamp monotonicity and log any flips.
corey: Also try an adaptive reclaimer throttle that uses recent pager-latency percentiles instead of fixed cadence. If page-ins exceed X ms, slow reclaim aggressiveness.
liam: Agreed. Plan: 1) add debug invariant + alerts, 2) experiment with adaptive reclaim backoff, 3) run long-context 2h soak with increased reuse_window and monitor mem/latency tradeoffs.
anya: I'll run the staged experiments and drop perf flamegraphs here.
dev-bot: perf-run queued: job/4182, ETA ~12m.
julia: If adaptive helps we can try hybrid policy: FIFO for fragmentation control + LRU scoring for reinserts in hot buckets.
prashant: Also add a small histogram on per-request page-in stalls so we can correlate to user-visible latency.
corey: Sounds good. Thanks team — please post short notes in the thread as you get results. :thumbsup:
